advances: Exact directional cap budget for one common continuous normal. The family of directional threshold cuts need not have a common point at a specified mixed-depth budget.

proof:
The lifted convex hull has exactly the three specified integer fibers. A convex combination at base zero has equal endpoint weights and therefore its endpoint contribution belongs to $(A+R)/2\subset K$. At the two extreme bases only their own generators can contribute. Through $(0,g)$ with continuous normal $u$, the base coefficient varies freely over all real $t$. The middle threshold is $s=u\cdot g$, and the two endpoint thresholds are $s+t$ and $s-t$, proving the directional cost expression. For fixed $s$, the endpoint sum is continuous in $t$ and equals one or the other whole endpoint mass for all sufficiently large positive or negative $t$. Minimizing over the intervening compact interval including those extreme values proves finite attainment. Pure base-normal through-caps include the middle fiber on the closed boundary and one full endpoint.

Apply the directional proof of 4fc403cf46f23e49 to the affinely independent endpoints $-1,1$ with weights $1/2,1/2$, keeping the same $u$ and using raw volumes. Its optimized cost is exactly $P$, and its inverse in root mass has a finite strictly decreasing branch between the full and empty plateaus. Specifically, if $\mathcal Q$ denotes its finite root-quantile, then $P(s)=m$ for $s\le\mathcal Q(m^{1/d})$ and $P(s)=0$ for $s\ge\mathcal Q(0)$. The first threshold is at least $\min_{x\in (A+R)/2}u\cdot x$ because every endpoint quantile is at least its minimum support and their averaged minimum supports equal that value. The second is $\max_{x\in (A+R)/2}u\cdot x$. By compatibility these are respectively at least $l_K$ and at most $h_K$. The predecessor's inverse gives continuity and monotonicity of $P$ between and across both plateaus. The ordinary profile $F$ is continuous because its boundaries have zero volume and strictly decreasing between its support values because every open slab there meets $\operatorname{int}K$. This proves the endpoints, strict decrease and continuity of $G$ on $[l_K,h_K]$. Outside that interval the respective constant values are $b+m$ and zero.

For each allowed allocation, $F(s)\le k$ holds exactly for $s\ge q(k)$ and $P(s)\le p$ exactly for $s\ge Q(p)$. At full mass the respective condition holds for every real threshold, which explains the $-\infty$ convention. At zero it starts at the appropriate upper support or endpoint support average. Thus each allocation yields $G(s)\le B$ above its displayed maximum and its maximum is at least $s_B$. Conversely take $k=F(s_B)$ and $p=P(s_B)$. Since $s_B$ is interior to the support interval of $K$, $q(k)=s_B$ and $Q(p)\le s_B$. This allocation attains the minimum. When $B<\min(b,m)$ the two terms of the maximum are continuous and strictly increasing and decreasing, respectively, as functions of $p$. Their difference is strictly increasing, so the maximum is minimized at the crossing or at $p=0$ when $q(B-p)$ dominates throughout and at $p=B$ when $Q(p)$ dominates throughout. On the saturated branch $p=m$ the other threshold alone remains.
statement:
Let $A,K,R$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, with $(A+R)/2\subset K$, at bases $-1,0,1$ respectively, using their disjoint summed volumes. Fix a unit continuous normal $u$, write $b=|K|$, $m=\min(|A|,|R|)$, and put
$$
F(s)=|K\cap\{u\cdot x\ge s\}|,\qquad
P(s)=\min_t\left(|A\cap\{u\cdot x\ge s+t\}|+|R\cap\{u\cdot x\ge s-t\}|\right),\qquad G=F+P .
$$
For $g\in K$, $G(u\cdot g)$ is the exact minimum mass of closed caps through $(0,g)$ with continuous normal $u$. Write $l_K,h_K$ for the minimum and maximum of $u\cdot x$ on $K$. The function $G$ is continuous and strictly decreasing on $[l_K,h_K]$, from $b+m$ to zero. For $0<B<b+m$ let $s_B$ be its unique threshold with $G(s_B)=B$. Then the directional lower budget condition on $g\in K$ is $u\cdot g\le s_B$.

For $0\le k<b$ let $q(k)$ be the ordinary cap quantile of $F$ with $q(0)=h_K$, and set $q(b)=-\infty$. For $0\le p<m$ let $Q(p)$ be the least threshold with $P(s)\le p$, and set $Q(m)=-\infty$. The exact allocation formula is
$$
s_B=\min_{\substack{k+p=B\\0\le k\le b,\ 0\le p\le m}}\max\{q(k),Q(p)\}.
$$
This minimum is attained. If $B<\min(b,m)$, use the crossing of $q(B-p)$ and $Q(p)$ on $[0,B]$ if it exists, or the minimizing endpoint otherwise. When $p=m$ is feasible its candidate value is $q(B-m)$. Pure base-normal through-caps have masses $b+|A|$ and $b+|R|$.
title: Exact directional budget allocation for an actual three-fiber source
